notes: The header pins were read from the images. The red wire goes to physical pin 1 (3V3.1), the green wire to pin 7 (GPIO4), and the black wire to pin 6 (GND.1). In the buzzer image, the second green wire goes to pin 11 (GPIO17, matching Buzzer(17) in the code), and the second black wire goes to pin 9 (GND.2).
The catalogue has no 1µF capacitor, so capacitor-10uf (POS/NEG) is used with value=1uF.

Breadboard holes follow the buzzer image, which has columns 1-30 left to right and rows f-j on top (bank 'b'). Red wire at 1b.f, green at 3b.f, black at 5b.f. The LDR legs are at 1b.j and 3b.j. The capacitor's positive leg is at 3b.i and its negative leg at 5b.i. The buzzer's black leg (pin 1, negative) is at 28b.j and its red leg (pin 2, positive) is at 30b.j.

The LDR and capacitor are placed in separate rows (j and i), as the images show, so their legs share the column strips 1 and 3. This gives 3V3 to LDR, then the LDR to the capacitor positive leg and GPIO4, and the capacitor negative to GND, as the text describes.
The two buzzer wires make 5 jumpers in total, where the parts list names only 3. The images are treated as the authority.
The laser pointer, drinking straw and speaker alternative are not electrical parts and are omitted.
